title: Easy Bruising / Bleeding
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with excessive bleeding after minor trauma, easy bruising, hemarthrosis (bleeding into joints — knees, ankles, elbows), and prolonged PTT with normal PT and normal platelet count. Hemophilia A is X-linked recessive deficiency of Factor VIII. Severity: mild (5-40% FVIII), moderate (1-5%), severe (<1%). PTT is prolonged (intrinsic pathway), PT normal (extrinsic pathway intact), platelets normal. Mixing study: PTT corrects (rules out inhibitor). Factor VIII assay confirms low activity. Treatment: factor VIII concentrate (recombinant preferred) for bleeding episodes or prophylaxis. Desmopressin (DDAVP) for mild hemophilia A (releases stored VIII and vWF). Avoid aspirin, NSAIDs, IM injections. Genetic counseling (X-linked).
chief_complaint: Joint bleeding, easy bruising, prolonged PTT
